text:
Samir Patel: Quick docs PR opened to clarify SOC2 audit-log section — mostly KMS wording + SDK example parity. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/842
Jules Huang: taking a look
Ravi Kapoor: quick q — should we use 'customer-managed keys (CMK)' or call out 'KMS/HSM' directly in the public docs?
Samir Patel: I switched to 'customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)' in the draft, but legal suggested simpler phrasing. Wanna align before we merge.
Maria Gomes (Legal): Hi — legal prefers 'customer-managed keys (CMKs)' and a parenthetical like 'e.g., KMS or HSM' to avoid vendor names. Also add a brief line about required access controls.
Jules Huang: ok will update. Also noticed the Python snippet under "audit export" uses client.export_logs(redact=True) while the Go example calls client.Export(ctx, Opts{Redact: true}). Method names diverged after the SDK refactor. We should make them consistent or explicitly versioned.
Samir Patel: Good catch. I left them as-is because the SDK surface changed. Would it be better to show high-level pseudocode instead of exact method names?
Ravi Kapoor: I'd rather keep copy-paste accurate examples. If we show pseudocode, customers will try to run it and fail. If APIs differ, show both and label with SDK version.
Maria Gomes (Legal): Agreed with Ravi. Examples should be accurate. If we include multiple variants, mark them as "Python SDK vX.Y" / "Go SDK vA.B". Also add note that examples assume default key policies and customers should consult their KMS provider.
docs-ci: build / docs:pr/842: succeeded :white_check_mark:
Jules Huang: plan: - change phrasing to "customer-managed keys (CMK) — e.g., KMS or HSM" - add a short note about tenant-scoped keys - normalize snippets (add version tags) - add a tiny table for encryption-at-rest / in-transit / audit-export
Samir Patel: one more nit — retention section currently says "7 years" in a sample. Legal asked we rephrase to be policy-driven and show a hosted default.
Maria Gomes (Legal): For docs examples, recommend: "default retention: 1 year (hosted); configurable per contract; enterprise customers may require longer retention to meet their compliance obligations."
Ravi Kapoor: also add an example CLI export with redaction flag: `redwood logs export --redact-sensitive --since 2024-01-01`
Jules Huang: adding curl + python + go snippets. Python snippet draft below — sanity check pls:
Jules Huang: ```python
from redwood import AuditClient
client = AuditClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_KEY")
client.export_logs(start_ts=1700000000, redact_sensitive=True, kms_key_id="projects/xxx/locations/xxx/keyRings/yyy/cryptoKeys/zzz")
```
Samir Patel: please replace actual GCP-ish path with a clear placeholder: `projects/PROJECT/locations/REGION/keyRings/NAME/cryptoKeys/KEY`
Jules Huang: done
Ravi Kapoor: LGTM on snippet names. @Maria Gomes (Legal) can you give final ok on the phrasing? If legal ok I'll merge and add a redirect for the old snippet link.
Maria Gomes (Legal): OK from legal — please add a one-line PR note: "Legal review: 2026-03-20 by M. Gomes" in the PR description.
Samir Patel: thanks. @Jules please ping when PR updated. I can queue a quick sanity run on the docs staging site.
Jules Huang: updated PR 842 — pushed. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/842/files
docs-ci: build / docs:pr/842: staging preview deployed — https://staging.docs.redwood.ai/audit-logs#kms
Ravi Kapoor: approving in GH
Jules Huang: thanks all :tada:
Samir Patel: merging in 10m unless objections
Maria Gomes (Legal): no objections
Samir Patel: merged. changelog note: "clarified CMK wording; added SDK-aligned examples; clarified retention default"
